title: Meta's Black Friday price spike will start from a higher floor
dek: Eight sources point the same way: Meta was already dearer than last year before Q4, the midterms added about 10% on top, and Black Friday adds a spike on that. The brands that came out ahead in 2025 judged the week on cost per purchase, not CPM.
body: Before November even starts, Meta is more expensive than a year ago. Northbeam's weekly CPM has been running about 24% above last year, and Meta's own earnings show the average price per ad up 14% in Q3. Common Thread's brands paid $17.13 in October 2025 and $21.55 in November, a 26% jump in a single month.

The midterms made the base higher still. Across Haus brands, Meta CPMs in the typical US market ran about 10% above last year from 1 October to Election Day, in safe markets as well as contested ones (New York +9%, Los Angeles +8%, Detroit +12%, Anchorage +19%). The rise came early, +10% in September, and conversion rates did not climb to offset it, leaving pixel-attributed efficiency about 8% worse than in August. Google CPCs rose about 4% and YouTube CPMs 6%, and Haus says prices had not normalized going into the BFCM run-up.

Black Friday stacks a spike on that base. Lebesgue tracked the median Meta CPM at 84% above its September level on Black Friday 2025, with fashion and footwear up 66% and home up 116%. Curtis Howland, who runs more than $5M a month on Meta, says his Black Friday day-one CPMs ran 45% above the week before. Triple Whale's BFCM average was $22.26, up about 7.8% on 2024.

But the expensive week was not the bad week. In the same Lebesgue data, cost per purchase fell 20% over Black Friday week because conversion rates rose 48%. Rising prices haven't stopped scaling this autumn either: Phil Kiel's biggest accounts raised spend 21% from September to October while CPA fell 3% and purchases rose 23%. Northbeam's caution is the exception: Black Friday was the one BFCM day where efficiency fell in 2025.

What to do with it: set Black Friday-week guardrails on CPA or new-customer CAC, not CPM; expect CPMs 45 to 85% above their pre-peak level; and fund prospecting in the first half of November, judged on lagged attribution, so the audience is already warm when prices peak. Howland's day-by-day split is one template: 100% of the BFCM daily budget Monday to Wednesday, 120% on Thanksgiving, 150 to 200% on Black Friday and Cyber Monday, 130% over the weekend.
sources: Haus (Tyler Horner) via Olivia Kory on X, 10 Nov 2026

title: Meta's problem going into Black Friday is conversion, not cost
dek: Meta CPMs have gone flat week to week, but Northbeam's weekly index shows Meta conversion rate falling three weeks running while click-through climbs. Its own analyst says conversion rates are at record lows. ROAS is holding, and Google is quietly taking share.
body: Cost has stopped being the headline. In Northbeam's Media Buyer Index for the week ending 1 November, Meta CPM moved -0.11% week over week and CPC fell 4.87%. CPMs are still about 24% above last year on Northbeam's weekly chart, but the week-to-week climb has paused for now.

Conversion is where it's slipping. Meta's conversion rate fell in each of the last three weekly readings: -1.63% (w/e 18 Oct), -2.88% (w/e 25 Oct) and -5.05% (w/e 1 Nov). Over the same three weeks click-through rose each time, by 5.35%, 2.17% and 4.86%. In the latest week new-customer CAC rose 1.50%.

Northbeam's Bryan Bumgardner reads the same pattern across about $6B of spend from 1,000 Northbeam customers: Meta conversion rates are at record lows while ROAS is better than ever. His explanation is that Meta now optimises toward clicks, which sends more, less-qualified traffic to the site. The index agrees on the ROAS side: Meta ROAS was up in all three weeks (+0.66%, +3.85%, +1.54%).

Google is picking up the slack. Its budget share in the index rose from 16.51% (w/e 18 Oct) to 18.00% (w/e 1 Nov), while Meta's slipped 0.74 points to 55.25% in the latest week. Google also opened Promotion Mode in beta, which lets Search and Performance Max campaigns lower their target ROAS for sales running 3 to 14 days.

What to do: treat the landing page as the Black Friday lever, because more clicks are reaching it and fewer are converting. Send new-customer signals back to Meta so it can find buyers, not just clickers. And keep a Shopify baseline for conversion rate, since Meta's on-device measurement switches on 12 November and will lift reported conversions for reasons unrelated to the site.
sources: Northbeam Media Buyer Index, w/e 18 Oct to 1 Nov
Northbeam, Black Friday Survival Guide (w/e 1 Nov index)
Direct to Consumer, Google Promotion Mode

title: Meta is changing how it measures, builds and reports ads in the three weeks before Black Friday
dek: Five Meta changes land between 28 October and 12 November. One deadline has gone away. The rest mean more conversions reported, more AI-made creative and finer reporting, just as budgets peak.
body: Measurement moves first. On 12 November Meta switches on "Measure conversions on customer devices" in Events Manager for every account. Common Thread cites early Meta tests showing up to 15% more attributed purchases for Advantage+ Sales campaigns. Pilothouse, via the DTC Newsletter, says leave it on but take a 7, 14 and 28-day baseline against Shopify first. Either way, Meta-reported ROAS will step up mid-month for reasons that have nothing to do with the ads.

Creative is being made for you. Since 2 November Image Animation, Video Expansion and Catalog-to-Video are on by default in new Advantage+ campaigns, so static product shots can run as video. Meta says its Andromeda and GEM delivery upgrades lifted conversions 15.7% and clicks 8.3% (as reported by Common Thread), and the takeaway from all of it is that the creative is now the targeting.

Reporting gets finer. Since 28 October Ads Manager breaks out seven metrics, including spend, CTR, CPA and ROAS, per individual creative in Advantage+ Shopping, Flexible and Dynamic Creative ads. Since 19 October API partners can also pair a creative with an age and gender range inside one ad set, though Meta has published no results for it.

The deadline that disappeared: Meta's new Commercial and Self-Serve Ad Terms, which would have made advertisers solely liable for AI-generated creative from 20 November, were delayed indefinitely on 3 November after EU and UK regulators opened inquiries. The March 2024 terms still apply. That removes a legal deadline, not the need to review what the AI makes.

What to do: baseline your Meta-vs-Shopify gap before 12 November and don't make structural changes in the two weeks after it; audit which Advantage+ Creative enhancements are on, ad by ad; use the new per-creative breakdown to pick Black Friday winners instead of a third-party tool.
sources: DTC Newsletter, 28 Oct (Pilothouse on conversion counting)

title: BFCM 2026: a bigger season, a tighter shopper, an earlier start
dek: Forecasters expect a record season ($275.1B online, Adobe), but most of the growth is price. Shoppers are starting earlier, discounts are anchored at 20 to 40%, and Canadian budgets are shrinking even as Black Friday stays the day that matters.
body: Adobe forecasts US online holiday spend of $275.1B (+6.7%), with Cyber Week at $47.5B and Black Friday the fastest-growing day at $12.9B (+9.2%). Bain expects the BFCM weekend to grow almost twice as fast as the season.

Underneath, unit demand is flat. In 2025 Salesforce saw US Cyber Week orders grow just 1% while prices rose, and this October's consumer sentiment reading was 48.0. Value framing (bundles, gifts with purchase, tiered offers) will do more than deeper discounts: the average Black Friday discount held at 28% last year and 45% of shoppers say 20 to 40% off is enough.

Timing has moved earlier. 71% of shoppers plan to buy before Black Friday and 28% expect their budget to be spent by the end of October. Owned channels carry the peak days (email and SMS were 43% of Klaviyo merchants' revenue), and AI referrals, though small, are growing fastest of any source.
In Canada, budgets are down 6.5% (RCC/Leger) to 14% (Deloitte), but 88% of shoppers rank Black Friday in their top three days and 58% of those affected by trade tensions are avoiding US brands.
sources: The full briefing, sourced line by line
